newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia rubber down at close despite Tokyo rise.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia rubber down at close despite Tokyo rise.

text.p: Malaysian rubber prices weakened further at close on continuing lack of consumers demand, despite gains in Tokyo, dealers said.

"Buyers are still not taking active positions due to the strike by the Goodyear Tire," a dealer at a trading firm, adding that the strike has worsened market situation and consumers are likely to keep at the sidelines until the strike is resolved.
Producers are quoting lower levels in order to attract overseas, they said.
Trading houses offered SMR 20 at 260 cent/kg, SMR CV at 331, SMR L at 311, SMR 5 at 272, SMR 10 at 260 and drum latex at 228.
The Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board said May RSS1 buyer ended 1.50 cents down at 278 cents ($1.11) and May SMR20 buyer was down 3.50 cents at 262.50.
The INRO five-day moving average was Malaysian/Singapore cents per kg was 210.94 on April 25 against 212.41 on April 24.
The daily indicator price was 208.84 against 209.44.
